scores.design: Commons — serverless file-based coordination ledger (single-writer-per-file, Lamport fencing, mailboxes, persisted pause phases with replay cache, tiered generator context)
scores.strongest_idea: One invariant — no file ever has two writers — turns any dumb transport (iCloud/Dropbox/Syncthing dir, or per-device `refs/jevcode/<deviceId>` read with `git cat-file --batch`) into a correct, conflict-free coordination bus with zero listeners, while the existing seatbelt already makes the ledger unforgeable and unreadable by sandboxed commands (src/sandbox/seatbelt.ts:102-104 default write-deny, :169-170 read-data deny on `~/.jevcode`). Records are self-checksummed so torn/half-synced files are skipped, staleness is the reader's clock + Lamport `(n, deviceId)` for order, and every fact (overlap, hash equality, branch equality, boot-time pid-reuse check) is code with Jev only judging the conflict. The `cache/step-<n>.json` replay (proposal + target sha256s + partial text + llm round cache) makes `pause now` free to resume and is gated by a hash fact (`[r]` absent when any target changed) — DESIGN.md:1471's 'no proposal is ever replayed' is deviated deliberately and safely. 38 enumerated corner cases each carry detection + recovery (pid reuse via boot time, `.icloud` placeholders as `unknown` not stale, ENOSPC/ESTALE/ETIMEDOUT never fatal, sharedDir-inside-workspace refused, duplicate deviceId adoption, case-insensitive overlap, submodule superKey, forked runs exit 2 on the higher stamp).
scores.fatal_flaw: Exclusivity is advertised but only advisory: (a) same device, two sessions can both pass the in-memory `overlap()` inside the 100 ms fs.watch debounce + async lease write and both execute — fencing re-judges only 'at the NEXT coordinate point; the step in flight is never interrupted', so two `edit`s of one file on one branch both land and are caught post hoc by `released.changed` hash compare; (b) cross-device, iCloud upload latency (minutes idle) exceeds `ttl+slack` (165 s), so a live peer's exclusive lease reads stale and is ignored (case 11 admits this). Two secondary holes undercut stated guarantees: the `repoKey` cache at `<commonDir>/jevcode-repokey` sits inside the git dir, which for a main tree is under the workspace and therefore sandbox-WRITABLE (seatbelt.ts:104 allows `subpath ws`; git denies at :120-127 cover only config/hooks/config.worktree/modules) — a prompt-injected `run` can forge the key and hide the session from peers, contradicting 'a forged record can only make us more cautious'; and the essential-set mirror copy is described as 'inside the IIFE', which `runStep` awaits before every execute (engine.ts:2202), so a hung NFS/iCloud `copyFile` (no fs timeout) would stall the next step.

scores.design: Switchboard — per-device coordinator daemon (`jevcode coord`) over a unix socket: in-memory registry + push-fed client mirrors, advisory leases default, daemon-routed pause/resume/end, engine agents registered like sessions, code-first compaction
scores.strongest_idea: Socket-open == live for same-device sessions: process death (SIGKILL, OOM) closes the socket, so the daemon marks the session `gone`, releases leases and keeps `touched`/`stage`/`action80` for 10 min — no pid-reuse ambiguity (lock.ts:26-35 EPERM=alive), no heartbeat guessing, sub-second peer visibility, and the per-step claim check is a synchronous Map lookup on a push-fed mirror. Around it: advisory-default claims that record a fact on the StepRecord and a prompt hint but never block (the Claude-sessions 'heads-up' model), a strict mode that holds the proposal INLINE at the pre-execute gate for ≤ 60 s wakeable by `lease:released` (no rule-1 re-buy), `BlockingAnswer 'pause'` so a pause during an open pane still ends as resumable `human_pause`, a `bench:<benchId>` exclusive lease closing the tasks.jsonl race (runner.ts:435, :718-719), monotonic-clock arrival stamps for cross-device staleness, and a deterministic code-fold compaction (Objective/Completed/Active/Blocked/Files/Tests/Notes) that is free and testable with LLM summaries opt-in.
scores.fatal_flaw: The daemon is a token-gated control plane that a sandboxed, generator-proposed command can reach by default. Verified: the seatbelt is `(allow default)` and denies `network*` only under `noNetwork` (seatbelt.ts:183), whose default is `false` (src/config/defaults.ts:126), so `connect()` to `$TMPDIR/jevcode-coord/coord.sock` is permitted; the bearer `token` lives in `~/Library/Application Support/jevcode/` — outside HOME_SECRET_SUBPATHS (`.config/jevcode`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.config/gh`, seatbelt.ts:66-67) and outside the `~/.jevcode` read-data deny (:169-170). A prompt-injected `run` step can therefore `cat` the token, `hello`, then `cmd end`/`cmd resume` every run on the device (spawning detached `jevcode run --resume` processes under `remoteControl:'allow'`), grab exclusive `own` leases to deny peers, and read the registry's 200-line transcript rings of OTHER runs — regressing the seatbelt's explicit invariant that 'other runs' prompts and outputs stay private' (seatbelt.ts:164-168). On Linux there is no sandbox at all. Secondary: `journal.jsonl` (durable mailbox) is written under `~/.jevcode/coord/`, so a synced `~/.jevcode` makes two daemons append to one file — the exact shared-append failure the design forbids for the bridge; daemon version skew after an upgrade and `start.lock` cleanup after a daemon crash are unspecified; the corner-case table is truncated after case 6 so cases beyond could not be credited.

grafts: From Switchboard: make claims advisory by default (`coordination.default: 'proceed'` → heads-up notice + `StepRecord.coord.conflicts` fact + next-step prompt hint; `ask`/`wait`/`worktree` opt-in). This meets 'do not block one another' literally, removes a Jev call + latency per conflict in the common case, and keeps Commons's Jev-judged `choice` for strict mode.

From Switchboard: at the `coordinate` gate, hold the proposal INLINE for a bounded strict wait (≤ `coordination.strictWaitMs`, default 60 s, wakeable by the watcher seeing the lease released/expired) before falling back to the rule-1 discard + `cache/step-<n>.json` replay — engine.ts:2203-2208 today discards when `this.blocked !== null`, so the pane path alone would re-buy or round-trip through replay.

From Switchboard: widen `BlockingAnswer` with `'pause'` so `/pause` while a blocking pane is open (jev-unreachable, spend-limit, drift, lease-conflict) resolves the pane and finishes as resumable `human_pause` — Commons's per-stage `pause({at:'now'})` aborts stage controllers only, and an awaited pane (engine.ts:1096-1098) is not a stage.

From Switchboard: default compaction to the deterministic code fold (`context.compaction: 'code'|'llm'|'off'`, default `'code'`: Objective/Completed/Active/Blocked/Files/Tests/Notes from plan, fileCache, lastTestRun, harnessProblems and one-line folded entries); keep Commons's generator-call summary as `'llm'` and its Jev-kept items on top. Free, testable, no 2–5 % spend surprise, works in jev-only.

From Switchboard: file memory with `sha12` per cached file and a zero-cost `read` of an unchanged file already in view — the execute stage answers `unchanged since step N (sha …); contents are in Files in view` without touching the generator budget; mark peer-changed files from `released.changed` under `## Files changed by other sessions`.

From Switchboard: close the bench race Commons filed as an open question — a `<benchDir>/bench.lock` O_EXCL per benchId using the existing acquireRunLock recipe (lock.ts:91-126), refusing a second `bench --resume` with the holder pid (runner.ts:435 append chain vs :718-719 rewrite).

From Switchboard: stamp foreign records with the receiver's monotonic arrival time (`performance.now()` at fold) and compute cross-device staleness from that, not from the record's wall `beatAt` vs the reader's wall clock — a local clock jump can then never flip a peer live/stale; keep Lamport stamps for order and the 5-min skew flag for display only.

From Switchboard: keep a dead run's `stage`/`action80`/`touched` visible for 10 min after its heartbeat goes stale so the resume card and `sessions who` can say `crashed during step 8 (propose, 41 s in); step 8 restarts` — Commons has `state.interrupted` (types.ts:944) but no 'what was in flight' banner for a SIGKILLed run.

Fix in Commons: move the `repoKey` cache out of `<commonDir>` (sandbox-writable for a main tree, seatbelt.ts:104) to `~/.jevcode/sessions/repokeys/<sha16(realpath(commonDir))>.json`, or validate `^[0-9a-f]{16}$` and recompute on any mismatch — never trust a key read from a path a sandboxed command can write.

Fix in Commons: mirror/essential-set copies and lease writes must ride their own promise chain with a per-op timeout (`Promise.race` with 5 s, classify ETIMEDOUT/ESTALE/ENOTCONN as `offline`) and must never be awaited by `pendingCheckpoint`, because `runStep` awaits that IIFE before every execute (engine.ts:2202) — a hung network FS otherwise stalls the run; only the ≤ 4 KiB local heartbeat may sit inside the IIFE.

Fix in Commons: after writing its own `exclusive` lease, re-fold the peer's lease dir once (≤ 2 ms, in-memory + one readdir of ≤ 2 KiB files) before `takePreImages`; if a lower-stamp overlapping lease appeared in the window, re-run the judgment NOW rather than at the next coordinate point — turns the sub-100 ms same-device double-claim into a pre-execute decision instead of a post-hoc hash conflict.

Fix in Commons (defensive, cheap): add `coordination.sharedDir`, any `git` transport work dir and `~/.jevcode/sessions/commons` to the seatbelt `readDenies` like `configDirs` (seatbelt.ts:157-162) so a sandboxed command cannot even read peers' task titles/paths from the mirror; refuse `sharedDir` under the workspace, runTmp, runHome or any `extraWritableRoots`.

scores.design: Commons — serverless file-based coordination ledger (heartbeats, fenced path leases, mailboxes, single-writer-per-file) + persisted pause/resume/end phases + opencode-style two-window context
scores.strongest_idea: The single-writer-per-file invariant (each device writes only commons/<deviceId>/**, every reader folds) makes any dumb sync a correct transport with no merge conflicts, and rides primitives the codebase already has verbatim: tmp+rename (src/core/atomic.ts:19-62), append-only fold (src/session/index.ts:288-389), fs.watch + 100 ms debounce (src/tui/useGitHead.ts:1-30), the read-denied ~/.jevcode (src/sandbox/seatbelt.ts:157-164), the cli-only source gate (src/session/index.ts:447-450). Paired with `pause now` that persists proposal + target hashes + llm round cache to cache/step-<n>.json so /resume replays instead of re-buying a 300 s generator call — the one pause feature users will feel.
scores.fatal_flaw: Breadth: W0–W4 is ~5k new LOC spanning three sync transports (local, shared-dir mirror, per-device git refs), scrypt pairing + HMAC, worktree relocation + child runs, a mailbox, a prompt file cache, compaction and kept items, all landing together; the new 'coordinate' StageName member (src/core/types.ts:240) ripples through every exhaustive switch and the stage:start/end transcript lines, and the proposed Esc-chord change collides with the pinned `Esc pauses · Esc Esc aborts` (docs/TUI-DESIGN.md:24, :252, :414 — the design's anchor DESIGN.md:1767-1786 is the shutdown section, not the chord). Cross-device liveness is TTL-over-sync (45 s + 120–180 s slack; iCloud can be minutes), so cross-device fencing is post-hoc hash comparison, not prevention — honest, but it means 'never block one another' is advisory off-device.

scores.design: Switchboard — per-device coordinator daemon (`jevcode coord`) over a unix socket: in-memory registry + leases + mailbox, daemon-routed pause/resume/end, engine agents registered like sessions, generous window with code-first compaction
scores.strongest_idea: Liveness = an open socket: process death closes it, so no TTL, no pid-reuse guessing (src/session/lock.ts:26-35 EPERM = alive), leases release instantly and peers see what was in flight. `pause --now` as `AbortError('human_pause')` through the existing shared controller + one line in classifyAbort (src/loop/stop.ts:41-45) is the smallest correct change; `BlockingAnswer 'pause'` fixes the real gap that a pane already awaited (engine.ts:1094-1110) cannot be paused today; code-first deterministic compaction is free and testable.
scores.fatal_flaw: The daemon is reachable from inside the sandbox. The seatbelt is `(allow default)` with `(deny network*)` only under --no-network (src/sandbox/seatbelt.ts:183), unix-socket connect is not a file-write, and the bearer token under ~/Library/Application Support/jevcode/ is in none of the read-deny lists (seatbelt.ts:66-67, :153-164 cover ~/.jevcode, .config/jevcode, .ssh, .aws, .config/gh, .netrc, configDirs). A generator-proposed `run` command of the same uid can read the token, connect, `cmd end all`, forge claims/hand-offs that the next prompt's hints line feeds back to the model, and the detached daemon inherits the process env (API keys) for no reason. The codebase has zero daemon/socket precedent, a second state dir outside JEVCODE_HOME breaks the hermetic temp-home pattern the r3 workflow relies on, and hermetic test/perf/pty runs sharing $TMPDIR would share one daemon. (Corner cases and security sections were truncated in the input; scored on what is visible.)

grafts: Pause-now via the SHARED controller, not per-stage controllers: when currentStage ∉ {execute}, `controller.abort(new AbortError('human_pause'))` and add the `'human_pause'` branch to classifyAbort (src/loop/stop.ts:41-45) so the rule-1 discard, exit 4 and no-`--force` resume fall out of existing code; during execute set pauseRequested and commit under rule 3 as Commons specifies. Keep Commons' cache/step-<n>.json write in markLastResort/finish for replay.

Widen BlockingAnswer with 'pause' (src/core/types.ts:1134): a `/pause` while `blocked !== null` resolves the awaited pane (engine.ts:1158-1214) and the loop maps it to finish('human_pause') — resumable — instead of exiting with the pane's stop code (Commons leaves a pane already awaited un-pausable).

Advisory-by-default claims: `coordination.claims = 'advisory' | 'strict' | 'off'` (default advisory) — a conflict is a fact (StepRecord.coord?.conflicts, a `notice kind:'coordination'`, a prompt hints line, and ≤ 8 × 200 chars in Jev's risk state) and never blocks; Commons' Jev Choice + wakeable `lease-conflict` blocker becomes the `strict` path. Matches how the coordinating Claude sessions actually work (know, warn, heads-up, never block) and saves one Jev call per conflicting step.

Code-first compaction as the default (`context.compaction = 'code' | 'llm' | 'off'`): a pure fold of task/plan.done/plan.remaining/harnessProblems/fileCache/lastTestRun/one-line step notes — deterministic, free, unit-testable; Commons' opencode-template generator call becomes the opt-in `'llm'` with fallback to code; keep Commons' Jev-kept items.

fileMemory zero-cost reads: record {sha12, bytes, readAt, editedAt} per file at commit (hashes already in post/<step>.json, src/checkpoint/images.ts) and execute a `read` of an unchanged file whose content is still in the tiered history as `unchanged since step N (sha …); contents are in Recent steps → step N` — complements Commons' prompt file cache and kills the re-read loop measured in experiments/results/glm-jev-off-baseline.md:224-231.

Session-start 'newcomer' pane: before store.create (engine.ts:3097-3098) fold the ledger for live heartbeats on the same repoKey+branch and show the peer's state (label, step/stage, touched files, spend, last beat) with `[j] join (advisory)  [w] wait  [t] worktree  [q] don't start`; default `join` under --plain/--no-input/--json. Commons only coordinates per step and would let two runs start silently.

Explicit target grammar for every control command, with a shell twin: `<runId8> | <sessionId8> | <title prefix> | me | all | tree | repo | device:<label>` for `/pause [now]`, `/end`, `/tell`, and `jevcode sessions pause|end|tell <target>` from any shell — the routed message rides Commons' outbox; each applied remote command writes the index line with an additive `by: 'self' | 'peer:<sid8>' | 'device:<id8>'` field (≤ 512 B still, src/session/index.ts:446-471).

Bench safety in scope but file-based: an O_EXCL `bench.lock` per benchId (the acquireRunLock recipe, src/session/lock.ts:91-126) for `bench --resume` races on tasks.jsonl (src/bench/runner.ts:435, :718-719); coordination itself stays off for source !== 'cli'.

Automatic boot-time reasoning in the lock path and `sessions unlock`: a run.lock/heartbeat whose startedAt predates system boot (os.uptime()) is stale even when kill(pid,0) succeeds — no `--stale` flag needed (src/cli/sessions.ts:111-114 today refuses forever after pid reuse).

Keep the key table: `Esc` = pause at step, `Esc Esc` = abort (docs/TUI-DESIGN.md:24, :252, :414 and `/abort`); put pause-now on `/pause now` and a bound chord (default Ctrl-P) instead of moving abort to Esc ×3 — Commons' own alternative; drop the chord-change open question.

Resolve Commons' ownership question from the record: docs/research/tui/workflows/r3-implement.js:19 says the peer (harness) session owns src/loop/**, src/synth/**, src/provider/**, src/bench/** — so prompts.ts and core/limits.ts are harness-owned; src/session/** is frozen for TUI slots in TUI-DESIGN-3 §7.2 (docs/TUI-DESIGN-3.md:1336), so lock.ts/index.ts changes need an explicit owner assignment before W1.

Keep the two-spawn budget (TUI-DESIGN §12.1, engine.ts:3040-3046): compute repoKey after run:ready / first frame on the heartbeat path (it is off the critical path anyway) with `git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD` (cheaper than --all on large repos) cached in <commonDir>/jevcode-repokey; heartbeat records before the key exists carry repoKey:null and are keyed by realpath until then.

Land in the order that proves the local case first: W0 contract + core/limits.ts → W1 local-only ledger (same-device sessions, lanes as leases, pause-now + replay, resume card) → W2 context policy → only then shared-dir mirror; defer git-ref transport, pairing/HMAC and the E2E relay idea entirely (remoteControl:'confirm' already holds the security floor without hmac, as Commons' own open question 6 notes).
